titulo: Bond Yields Surge and AI Jitters Shake Markets
resumo: October 2026 brought heightened volatility as soaring bond yields and mounting debt fears tested investor resolve. The S&P 500 managed a **+1.4% monthly gain** to reach 7757.17, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped **-3.2%** to 26008.86 amid rising scrutiny over artificial intelligence spending. Persistent inflation concerns pushed the US 10-year Treasury yield to 5.13% and spurred a broader global bond sell-off. Meanwhile, energy markets remained sensitive to geopolitical tensions, keeping Brent crude at $115.22 a barrel.

sumup.frase: Markets navigated **inflation pressures**, rising yields, and tech sector volatility during October.
sumup.porque: Rising bond yields and stubborn inflation kept investors on edge despite record-chasing equities.

drivers.texto: The US 10-year yield fell by -16bp over the month to settle at 5.13%, while the 2-year yield dropped -7bp to 4.81. Strong demand at recent Treasury auctions helped temporarily ease the relentless bond market sell-off.

drivers.factor: Tech sector and AI spending jitters
drivers.texto: The Nasdaq Composite fell -3.2% this month to 26008.86 as investors scrutinized heavy artificial intelligence infrastructure borrowing. Credit default swaps and debt concerns for major tech-linked firms weighed heavily on sentiment.
Euro area inflation held at 3.8% in September, while US price pressures remained elevated. Central banks maintained a careful stance, with the ECB deposit rate holding at 2.5%.
Brent crude stood at $115.22 a barrel, down slightly by -0.6% on the month but up +87.8% for the year. Supply concerns tied to Middle East disruptions kept energy costs near multi-year highs.
The S&P 500 climbed +1.4% on the month to 7757.17, supported by earnings optimism and sector rotation away from pressured technology names despite elevated macro headwinds.

themes.texto: Sustained economic resilience and fiscal worries have kept global bond yields near multi-decade highs. The US 10-year yield ended the period at 5.13%, down -16bp for the month, while euro area 10-year AAA yields retreated -20bp to 3.3844%. These elevated borrowing costs are rippling through mortgage markets and corporate debt structures.

The immense capital expenditure required for AI infrastructure is starting to worry credit markets. Investors are increasingly scrutinizing the debt loads of hyperscalers and data centre operators, leading to higher credit spreads and a temporary rotation out of high-flying technology shares.

With euro area inflation standing at 3.8% and Portugal's inflation at 3.6% in September, policymakers face a difficult balancing act. The ECB deposit rate remains at 2.5%, while average 12-month Euribor sits at 3.247%, maintaining pressure on household borrowing costs.

The US dollar maintained broad strength as the EUR/USD exchange rate fell -1.3% over the month to 1.1205. Meanwhile, Brent crude remained elevated at $115.22 a barrel, continuing to drive input costs higher for manufacturers and refiners globally.

questoes.porque: Debt-funded infrastructure spending is driving up credit default swaps and raising investor risk awareness.
questoes.sinais: Upcoming corporate earnings reports and specialized debt auctions.

questoes.porque: High oil and fuel prices threaten to feed into core inflation readings and squeeze household disposable incomes.
